match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the proactive versus reactive distinction: bus-forces-change covers where pressures for change come from, and bus-technological-change covers technology as a driver, so the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Forms of business change
card: Business change is any shift in how a business works. It might alter its products, processes, structure, people or technology.
change made before a problem arises, because managers expect or want something to happen. An example is updating a system before it starts to fail.
change made in response to a problem or event that has already happened. An example is replacing a system after it has failed.
The difference is timing. Proactive change comes before the trouble. Reactive change comes after it. Both are forms of change.
draft.remember: Proactive change acts before a problem. Reactive change responds to one.

a.q: Which situation is an example of proactive change?
opts: A bakery trials online ordering before sales start to fall
A bakery buys a new oven after its old one breaks down
A bakery changes its recipes after a spike in complaints
A bakery hires extra staff after a rival opens next door
a.why: The bakery acts before any problem has appeared, so the change is proactive. The other three each follow a problem or event that has already happened, so they are reactive.
a.clue: Look for the change that comes before any trouble.

b.q: Priya's gym in Geelong has steady profits. She adds a new app for bookings after a rival's app draws away many members. How is this change best described?
opts: Reactive, because it responds to the rival's app
Proactive, because the gym's profits are still steady
Proactive, because it adds new technology to the gym
Reactive, because it changes how the gym takes bookings
b.why: The change follows the rival's app and the loss of members, so it is a response to an event and is reactive. Steady profits do not make it proactive, because timing is judged against the event that prompted the change.
b.clue: Ask what happened first: the change or the loss of members.

a.best: A bakery trials online ordering before sales start to fall

b.best: Reactive, because it responds to the rival's app

problems.detail: The right option is the only one that says 'before'; the other three all say 'after'. With the clue ('comes before any trouble'), a student can match the keyword without understanding the idea. A distractor that also uses 'before', or a right option phrased without it, would test the concept better.
